input:
If I = integral((sin x + sin^3 x)/cos 2x) dx = P cos x + Q log|sqrt(2 cos x - 1)/sqrt(2 cos x + 1)| (where c is a constant of integration), then values of P and Q are respectively

Options:
A. 1/2, 3/(4sqrt(2))
B. 1/2, -3/(4sqrt(2))
C. 1/2, 3/(2sqrt(2))
D. 1/2, -3/(2sqrt(2))

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Integrate the expression and identify constants P and Q in the given final form.

given_information.integral: I = integral((sin x + sin^3 x)/cos 2x) dx
given_information.target_form: P cos x + Q log|sqrt(2 cos x - 1)/sqrt(2 cos x + 1)| + c

phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Substitute t = cos x and convert denominator using cos 2x = 2cos^2 x - 1.

key_formulas.substitution: t = cos x, -sin x dx = dt

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Transform to t-integral, split into simpler fractions, integrate, then compare coefficients.
logical_steps: Step 4: Match with P and Q form

step_4_back_substitute.equivalent_form: I = (1/2)cos x - (3/(4sqrt(2))) log|sqrt(2cos x-1)/sqrt(2cos x+1)| + c

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: After substitution and simplification, coefficient comparison gives P and Q exactly as in option B.
